key_insight: The ECMO-READY trial is testing whether pre-cannulated standby VA-ECMO can match prophylactic ECMO for safety and effectiveness during high-risk PCI while potentially avoiding unnecessary ECMO exposure.
clinical_relevance: If standby ECMO proves comparable, it could offer a more selective support strategy for complex PCI with fewer ECMO-related complications and lower resource use.
method: Prospective, multicenter, open-label randomized controlled trial at 8 sites in China
176 patients undergoing high-risk PCI randomized 1:1 to standby ECMO or prophylactic ECMO
Primary endpoint: 30-day composite of major adverse events; multiple procedural and resource-use secondary outcomes
evidence_signal: This is a trial protocol, so the abstract provides planned evaluation and sample size but no outcome data yet.
watch_item: Open-label design and the complexity of a broad composite endpoint may make interpretation and implementation dependent on local expertise and event definitions.
paper_title: Study protocol for a multicenter randomized controlled trial comparing standby versus prophylactic extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in high-risk percutaneous coronary intervention (ECMO-READY trial)
